ordered_diagnoses: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the iris
Primary central nervous system lymphoma with ocular involvement

s1.syndrome_frame: A vascularized iris mass with ciliary body involvement and anterior chamber angle involvement
salient_findings: 10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule
key_facts: Patient is a man in his late 60s
Presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
Slitlamp examination showed a vascularized iris nodule
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showed a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic lymphocytes
Lymphocytes were CD20+
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation showed no other involvement
Staging was T2N0M0

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a vascularized iris nodule with ciliary body involvement and biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of CD20+ lymphocytes is most consistent with iris lymphoma.

rejected.label: Uveal lymphoma
rejected.why: While uveal lymphoma could explain some of the findings, the specific involvement of the iris and the presence of a well-delineated nodule make iris lymphoma a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: MALT lymphoma of the iris
rejected.why: MALT lymphoma is a type of lymphoma that typically arises in the context of chronic inflammation, which is not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the iris
rejected.why: The biopsy results showed a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized lymphocytes, which is not typical of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma with ocular involvement
rejected.why: There is no mention of central nervous system involvement, and the staging was T2N0M0, indicating that the disease is localized to the eye.

gold: Primary B-cell mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma of the iris
